rationale.text: Tile the outer `i` dimension by 128 to create 8 independent row-groups (1024/128=8). This maps cleanly to the 30-SM device, giving 8×(j-tiles) thread-blocks that can be scheduled across SMs. 128 rows per tile also keeps L1 reuse high for elementwise ops.

Tile the inner `j` dimension by 128 to create 8 column-groups (1024/128=8). With 128 elements per tile, we get 64 total thread-blocks (8×8), which is 2× the SM count (30), ensuring good wave occupancy. The 128-wide inner tile will allow vectorized 128-bit loads (4×float32) along `j`.

Vectorize the `j` loop with width=4 to emit 128-bit vector loads/stores (float4). The `j` axis is the contiguous (row-major) dimension, so 4×float32 = 128-bit aligned accesses match the Ampere L1/L2 cache line structure and maximize memory bandwidth utilization for this memory-bound elementwise kernel.

Map tiled `i` outer loop to threadblock.x so each tile of 128 rows becomes an independent GPU thread-block. Combined with the `j` tiling, this generates 8×8=64 thread-blocks total — about 2 full waves across 30 SMs — keeping all SMs busy and hiding launch/scheduling overhead.
